title: SimCity 99 — Gameplay Depth Roadmap (10 independently-shippable milestones)
method: Six designer-critics audited the ACTUAL sim source per dimension against the SimCity 2000 gameplay bar, then synthesis -> a 3-lens adversarial panel (feasibility / fun / leverage) -> reconcile. The panel corrected numerous factual errors in the draft and added a milestone the draft was missing.
benchmark: SimCity 2000 coupled-systems depth plus tasteful modern city-builder norms, recreated clean-room in vanilla JS. Gameplay only — the visual bar lives in docs/graphics-quality-rubric.json (roadmap complete).
north_star: SimCity 99 should be a city you must keep GOVERNING — and one that keeps handing you new shapes to draw while it does. Every tile feeds one coupled spatial economy: distance to jobs decides which neighbourhoods grow and which starve, so layout is the core decision, and the player always has a real answer to a bottleneck (a road class hierarchy with ramps, a rail line with a train actually running on it) rather than only more of the same road. Land value is the tax base, so parks, clean air, schools and transit are investments with a payback period — and education is a decade-scale stock that unlocks cleaner, richer industry rather than a recurring bill with no reward. Services strain as the city expands, so every thousand new residents re-opens the budget fight; neglect leaves scars that cost money and time to undo, but the player always owns a campaign against them and a stabilizer keeps the spiral survivable. Hazard is the itemized bill for decisions visible on a risk readout beforehand, fought with an allowance always smaller than the fire front. All of it is legible IN the game from one source of truth: growthPass's own gate table, read back to the player as a per-tile verdict naming the single binding constraint with its proving number, RCI bars that decompose into their named signed contributors, and one honest approval number backed by a ranked, clickable problem list. Determinism is made REAL first — a seeded sim stream, not a stubbed Math.random — so every later byte-identity claim means something. Recreate SC2K's coupled depth and standing dilemmas clean-room, in pure vanilla JS with zero dependencies and no build step, 1997 flavor, versioned backward-compatible saves on one declared ladder.

rubric.pass_bar: Money is a standing decision, not a setting. Revenue is assessed on land value and zone wealth, so two cities of equal population but different quality differ in take by >=35%. The tax lever has a measured, single-peaked equilibrium-revenue curve on a PINNED reference city, and any multi-rate split is proven separable at equilibrium before it ships (demand.r keys on jobsAvail = jobs + 40 - pop*0.62, so soaking industry can silently strangle residential demand). Costs scale with what the city consumes, so an established city cannot net a permanent unattended surplus. Debt is a real ladder (chooseable principal/term, a ceiling tied to the assessed base, rating with memory) and insolvency is survivable via an owned stabilizer. Progression has a rung above Metropolis with at least one requirement beyond raw population.

The network's SHAPE matters. Trips seek destinations, so bottlenecks emerge from topology and a second crossing measurably drains the first — without collapsing every trip onto one canonical stripe. A road CLASS hierarchy exists: capacity costs money, footprint and neighbourhood land value, and grade separation needs ramps to touch the local grid. A legible commute stat responds to layout within months and feeds growth. Transit pays for where the line GOES, and the network is visibly alive (a train actually runs). Ports and terminals are connected infrastructure generating freight traffic and revenue, not power consumers with sprites.

Consequences persist and propagate. Decline has hysteresis: failure produces a state that does not snap back for free, costs money or time to reverse, and the player owns an active campaign against it rather than a cooldown. At least one slow stock rewards a decade-scale investment horizon and changes what the city can build. Demand is at least partly local. Waste, pollution and land value form closed loops the player outsmarts by placement rather than volume. Every shipped subsystem affects at least two others, and every new tile id passes an explicit anti-crosstalk audit against the documented `>= OV.ZR` power/fire idioms.

Services are an ongoing operation with a payoff, not a one-time stamp. Coverage scales against a load that grows with the city; funding sliders have measurable, opposite-signed effects on cost and effectiveness. Education and health are mechanically distinct with different payoffs — not summed at sim.js:1392/1709 and OR-gated at 1721 — and education returns something economic. Every service's coverage is on a minimap mode and in the query panel, and station placement is previewable before spending. At least one service building carries a genuine siting tradeoff.

Pressure is a curve coupled to play. Hazard rates are functions of coverage, crime, pollution, plant type and age, and exposure — visible on a risk readout BEFORE anything lands, with honest per-year odds matching the measured empirical rate. The player acts during an event under a scarce allowance that forces triage, and an in-progress event survives save/load. Aftermath persists economically. All shipped disaster kinds are reachable from the menu and usable as scenario pressure, and scenarios have a real difficulty axis.

Every rule the sim enforces is discoverable in-game, from ONE source of truth — the growth gate table the sim itself consumes, so a new gate cannot ship without its verdict. Any tile is inspectable without a tool switch and reports the ONE binding constraint in plain language with the proving number, including the soft stalls (demand below the upgrade threshold, negligible fit odds), not just the hard gates. The headline quality-of-life number is derived from real state and backed by a ranked problem list whose rows jump the camera to the worst cluster. RCI and budget gauges decompose into named, signed contributors. Transient warnings are not stomped by hover chrome. Advisory output is severity-ranked.

save_version_ladder: GP1b OWNS save v12 (implemented, verify + panel + fix complete, NOT yet marked shipped), establishing the ladder: every later state-adding milestone takes the next integer, the loader maintains backward compatibility for all earlier versions with defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards and NO hard version equality test, and normaliseHistory must be extended for any new history key (it builds from a hardcoded key list and DROPS unknown keys — the rule is now recorded in a comment at the function itself). v12 adds, after every v11 key so the v11 prefix stays character-stable: rng (four cursor ints), powerEpoch, trafficEpoch, sinceComplaint, powerDirty, and packU8-encoded traffic/unpow/fire (a four-mode raw / RLE / packbits / sparse-bitmask BYTE pack emitted as one base64 STRING per plane, shortest mode wins - the JSON-number packing it replaces cost +10.83% of the payload on the pinned reference city and breached the milestone's own <=5% save gate there while passing it on the sparser stress city). GP1a did NOT touch the save format.

loop_protocol.driver: /goal + /loop — each iteration runs the next todo milestone to completion via scratchpad/wf-milestone.mjs, ships it, and advances.
per_milestone_workflow: SHIP (smoke check, commit, bundle, artifact, push)
invariants: Each milestone is INDEPENDENTLY SHIPPABLE — stopping between any two leaves a coherent game.
New randomness via seeded/side streams; no per-frame Math.random in bakes.
Save-format changes follow the version ladder with backward-compatible loading.
Scenario winnability re-checked by every growth-touching milestone (they suppress equilibrium growth and stack multiplicatively).
Any new tile id gets an explicit anti-crosstalk audit against the >= OV.ZR power/fire/census idioms.
Zero console errors; perf within ~20% of baseline.

milestones.title: Growth Verdicts — the Gate Table & Tile Diagnosis
milestones.scope: SPLIT FROM THE ORIGINAL GP1 (which bundled three surgeries and was refuted by all three adversarial lenses on its first attempt). This half is PURE READ + UI: absolutely NO change to simulation behavior. (A) GATE TABLE: refactor growthPass in js/sim.js so its gates become an ordered DECLARATIVE TABLE that growthPass ITSELF consumes — same decisions, same order, same RNG draw count and order, byte-identical outcomes. This is a pure restructuring, not a behavior change. diagnoseTile(i) is a pure read walking that same table, returning {code, severity, text, evidence}. One source of truth, so later milestones ship their gates with a player-facing verdict for free and cannot desync. The table must cover what growthPass ACTUALLY does — verify each against the source, do not trust this list blindly: burning tile (precedes everything); unpowered decay (unpow > 6); no road access; water hard cap (fires at lvl >= 1, so it PRE-EMPTS the level-2 service cap); level-2 service cap (eduCov < 8 && medCov < 8); level-2 pressure gate (waterPressure < 0.9); gridlock eviction; DEMAND BELOW THE UPGRADE THRESHOLD (the branch is gated on dem > 0.15, so a tile at 0.10 stalls forever — the commonest invisible stall); NEGLIGIBLE FIT ODDS (the roll is rand < dem * fit * 0.42, where fit compounds landv/255, -crime/400, (1 - cong*0.75), the svc term and the pressure term — a blighted low-landv block passes every hard gate and still never upgrades); decline (dem < -0.25); else growing normally. Non-zone verdicts: unpowered pump, one-station line, plant past PLANT_WARN_AGE, unconnected special. (B) SURFACES: a verdict block at the top of openQuery, re-rendered on a ~500ms cadence; RCI bars that decompose on click into their named signed contributors (jobsAvail/220, taxMod, stadMod, svcMod, event mods, ordinance mods — all sitting visible in recomputeDemand and never shown to the player); a hover readout in a NEW status cell driven by UI.hover, NOT #sb-tool (which carries transient messages that a per-pixel mousemove would erase before they can be read — those keep their own cell and gain a message TTL); and a running drag-cost meter that is a PREVIEW which warns but never blocks (place() already returns {ok:false, reason:"funds"} and applyToolAt already plays Snd.denied()). EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the seeded-RNG substrate migration and any save-format change — those are GP1b. This milestone must NOT bump the save version.
milestones.player_facing_win: A player who zones a perfect block and watches it stall is finally told, in the game, exactly which gate is holding it — including the two invisible ones ('demand 0.10, needs 0.15' and 'upgrade odds ~0.3%/yr: land value 18, congestion 71%') — and can read any tile, and the RCI bars themselves, just by hovering.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM: because this is a pure refactor plus a pure read, 20 seeds x 600 ticks with Math.random stubbed identically on both sides produce 0 differing bytes in over/lvl/varnt/unpow/fire/traffic, identical pop/funds/jobs, and identical save JSON versus the pre-change baseline. The RNG draw count and order must be unchanged.

Gate-table fidelity, not self-reference: an instrumented growthPass logs the branch it actually short-circuits on; over 5,000 sampled tiles across 20 seeded cities, diagnoseTile names that same first gate with 0 mismatches, and each code is reproduced by a scripted city that trips exactly it.

The two invisible stalls are caught: a tile with 0 < dem <= 0.15 returns the demand-threshold code (never 'growing normally'), and a tile passing every hard gate whose fit-derived per-roll upgrade probability is < 0.005 returns the negligible-odds code with land value and congestion as its evidence numbers.

Verdict text is TRUE in every case it renders: WATER_CAP must not claim 'capped at level 1' on a level-2 lot; UNPOWERED must not claim an in-progress level loss on a lot whose own apply-guard prevents the decrement; a tile whose gridlock loss exceeds its upgrade odds must not read as a green 'ok'; and no verdict box appears at all on unzoned bare grass or open water.

Read-only and UI-safe: diagnoseTile performs zero sim writes and draws zero RNG (a write-trap proxy over every city array and an rng-call counter both report 0); no hover event overwrites a transient status message before its TTL expires; an open query dialog reflects a sim change within 600ms; zero console errors.

No save change and no perf regression: the save version stays v11 and round-trips byte-identically; sim tick and frame time on a matched developed 128x128 city stay within ~10% of the pre-change baseline — re-measure honestly rather than asserting.

milestones.title: Seeded Simulation Substrate — Make Determinism Real
milestones.scope: SPLIT FROM THE ORIGINAL GP1. Pure infrastructure, no player-facing feature. The shipped determinism invariant is not real: js/sim.js makes ~43 raw Math.random() calls across the whole tick path (growth sampling and every growth/decay roll, recomputeTraffic reservoir pick, road wear, fire spread, the disaster roll, complaint scanning), while mulberry32 serves only terrain and neighbor personalities. Byte-identity has so far been achieved by STUBBING Math.random, which makes it hypersensitive to draw count and order. Route every tick-path draw through named seeded sub-streams on city.rng (growth / traffic / fire / hazard), with cursors serialized. Save bumps to v12 with backward-compatible v11 loading, establishing THE version ladder for every later state-adding milestone. CRITICAL, carried from the first attempt where all three lenses refuted: powered[] is NOT serialized and is NOT a pure function of the saved world — recomputePower stamps it with rng.hazard() brownout and Y2K flicker cuts — and City.sinceComplaint is a second unserialized accumulator gating rng.hazard() draws. Both must be resolved (serialize them, or make the stamping a pure function of serialized state) or the determinism claim is hollow. This is the ONE authorized deliberate RE-PIN of the sim baseline; after it, "same seed produces the same city" is true UNSTUBBED and every later identity gate means something. The first attempt is preserved in git history at commit e5140a0 and may be mined for reference, but its measured regressions must not be inherited unexamined: an independent re-measure found the tick ~14% SLOWER while the implement pass claimed 22% faster, and the save payload grew ~57%.
milestones.player_facing_win: Two players who start the same seed and play the same moves get the same city — and saving and reloading no longer silently changes the simulation’s future.
quality_gates: Determinism is real: with Math.random left UNSTUBBED and global, two fresh runs from the same seed and input script produce byte-identical over/lvl/varnt/fire/traffic arrays, pop, funds and save JSON over 600 ticks.

Save/load is determinism-preserving: a save at tick 300, reloaded, reproduces the tick-600 state byte-identically. This requires every array the sim reads back to be serialized or a pure function of serialized state — powered[] and City.sinceComplaint must both be explicitly resolved and the resolution demonstrated.
No global draws remain on the tick path: an instrumented counter reports 0 global Math.random calls across 600 ticks on a stress city exercising growth, traffic, fire, wear, disasters and complaints.

The re-pin is bounded and declared: versus the pre-change baseline, pop/funds/jobs at ticks 100/300/600 across 20 seeds stay within +/-5% of the old distribution mean, and all shipped scenarios remain winnable (medal condition met in at least 8 of 10 seeded playthroughs of a scripted reference solution). The new baseline is pinned and COMMITTED to git as the reference for every later milestone.

Save-compat and honesty: a genuine v11 save loads at v12 with cursors seeded deterministically, resaves, round-trips idempotently, and continues 120 rollovers cleanly; the save payload size delta and the sim-tick perf delta versus baseline are both re-measured and reported honestly (tick within ~20%), not asserted.
No gameplay or visual change: sprites byte-identical, UI unchanged, zero console errors.

milestones.title: Working Ports — Wire the Airport & Seaport into the Economy
milestones.scope: Close the confirmed dead-content gap. sim.js:55-64 documents it in the code's own words: NUKE joined isPlant(), but 'AIRPORT and SEAPORT deliberately join NO predicate — behaves exactly like OV.STADIUM' — they render, draw power, and touch no demand, revenue, traffic or pollution path. Both now require power AND a road or rail tile adjacent to the footprint; an unconnected port produces exactly zero effect and says so on its own line in the query panel. SEAPORT: industrial demand bonus scaled by industrial jobs inside a catchment radius, monthly freight revenue proportional to served industry (bonus when rail touches the footprint), and a pollution source. AIRPORT: commercial demand bonus, tourism revenue scaled by mean land value and landmark pride in reach, and a directional NOISE penalty suppressing residential land value under its approach — so it wants commerce near and good neighbourhoods far. Both deposit freight/passenger trips onto load[] at their gate tiles, so a port generates real truck traffic on whatever street you connected it to (and once GP3 lands, that traffic has to traverse a network whose shape matters, upgrading the port from 'a building that pays a number' into a corridor commitment). New 'Ports & Terminals' budget row; query panel reports jobs served / earned last month / connection state. Costs, footprints and tier gates unchanged; no new OV ids, no save change. Effort re-rated 2->3: the directional noise map, the catchment scan, monthly revenue, the load[] deposits, the budget row and the query rows are six pieces, not two. All port code must draw ZERO RNG so the no-port identity gate is genuinely non-vacuous rather than accidentally shifting the seeded stream.
milestones.player_facing_win: The two most expensive buildings in the game stop being ornaments — a port becomes a specialization bet that pays only if you dedicate a corridor to it and site it where its smog or its approach noise costs you least.
quality_gates: A powered, road-connected seaport with >=200 industrial jobs in catchment raises demand.i by >=0.10 vs an identical control city and posts non-zero freight revenue within 1 rollover.
An unpowered or unconnected port produces zero demand delta, zero revenue and zero traffic delta, and the query panel names the specific missing prerequisite (power vs connection).

Airport tradeoff: demand.c rises >=0.08 while mean landv of residential tiles under the approach falls >=12 vs control, and the penalty is directional (tiles off-approach at equal distance fall <3); tourism revenue is monotone in mean land value across 3 test cities.
Ports generate traffic: mean load[] on road tiles within 5 of a working port is >=25% above the control city, and the increase is traceable to the port's gate tiles.

Non-vacuous identity: an rng-call counter proves the port code path draws zero RNG, and cities containing no airport or seaport are byte-identical to the GP1 pinned baseline across 600 ticks (all serialized arrays + save JSON) with save version unchanged.

Reversibility: bulldozing a port fully reverts every derived effect (demand bonus, revenue, noise, pollution, load deposits) within one recompute, leaving state byte-identical to a city that never had one; zero console errors.
milestones.implementation_note: 2026-07-27 IMPLEMENT phase (js/sim.js + js/ui.js only; no render/sprites/css, no new OV id, no save change). SHAPE: isPort() is a NEW predicate that adds nothing to and removes nothing from AIRPORT/SEAPORT's existing memberships (they still conduct, still count as powered consumers, stay brownout/Y2K/fire eligible, stay outside isPlant/isWaterOv/isMega). ONE PURE RECORD portRecord(a) (zero RNG, zero writes) is the single definition of a port and is consumed by recomputePorts, portsBudget, the three new INFRA_GATES rows and the query panel alike, so the panel cannot desync from the economy. recomputePorts() is a REBUILD pass filling the DERIVED, NEVER-SERIALIZED ports/portWork/portDemI/portDemC/portsRev/portsCost (plus noiseCov from stampAirportNoise and portDep from the traffic deposit); anchor discovery is FUSED into computeDemandParts' existing full-map loop, so GP2 adds no new O(n) per-tick scan. Demand folds as an APPENDED '+ this.portDemC' / '+ this.portDemI' term (never a re-association) and demandBreakdown gained the matching named part in the same source order. Traffic deposits through a deterministic bounded BFS (spreadPortTrips) over ROAD/WIREROAD from the gate tiles - never the reservoir walk, whose TRAFFIC hash domain would have made the zero-RNG gate vacuous. milestones.scope: This is the north star's central claim and it is promoted from rank 7 because everything ranked below it would otherwise be written against a growth model this replaces. Replace the blind 10-step random walk (recomputeTraffic, js/sim.js:1236-1270) for RESIDENTIAL trips: once per traffic pass, run ONE multi-source BFS over the road + live-rail graph seeded from every road tile serving a developed ZC/ZI, producing jobDist[] (hops to nearest job-serving road, 255 = unreachable). Residential trips then walk DOWN jobDist within a MAX_COMMUTE budget, depositing onto load[] at each step; trips exhausting the budget are 'stranded'. TWO CORRECTIONS the panel proved necessary. (1) A STRICTLY-downhill walk is a tie-break-deterministic shortest path — every trip from a neighbourhood collapses onto one canonical corridor and parallel streets sit at literal zero load, which looks wrong and makes the shipped animated cars (render.js:1188, which favor busy roads) bunch onto stripes. Instead choose among ALL neighbours with jobDist <= current-1, weighted by the seeded traffic sub-stream GP1 provides, so load spreads realistically while staying reproducible. (2) The draft's 'C/I trips keep the legacy walk so the change stays surgical' was false pre-GP1 — the reservoir pick at sim.js:1267 drew from the same global Math.random as the C/I trips, interleaved in one loop, so deleting residential walks would have shifted every subsequent C/I pick. GP1's named per-purpose sub-streams make the claim true and testable; this milestone hard-depends on that. Derive city.avgCommute (mean hops over arriving trips) and city.strandedShare; fold avgCommute into growthPass's residential fit and a mild demand.r damper, and add a minimum-job-reach gate on ZR upgrades above level 1 — registered in GP1's gate table so it ships with its own tile verdict for free. Ranked list correctness: for each perturbation the induced problem appears in the top 2 rows with a plausible naming percentage, and its Show-me button sets the documented minimap mode and centers the camera within 6 tiles of that metric's argmax tile.

milestones.title: Assessed-Value Taxation, the Debt Ladder & the Stabilizer
milestones.scope: Demoted from rank 2 by all three lenses: highest blast radius, largest save claim, and a DIAGNOSIS THAT WAS WRONG. sim.js:1503 is `taxMod = (7 - this.taxRate) * 0.05` — strictly LINEAR, not the 'flat-then-cliff' the draft described; and a headless rig showed an R-heavy config ALREADY produces a single-peaked curve peaking at 7% that would pass the draft's own Laffer gate on HEAD, while a serviced balanced rig shows revenue climbing monotonically to 13% ('set 13% and win' — the genuinely degenerate case). So the FIRST deliverable is a measurement spike on a PINNED reference city (committed seed, size, script, building mix) identifying which term binds equilibrium: taxMod, or `jobsAvail = jobs + 40 - pop*0.62` over 220 (sim.js:1516). THEN: replace the headcount formula (sim.js:2145 `pop*taxRate*0.28 + jobs*taxRate*0.18`, duplicated in the finance advisor's projection at advisors.js:373/394 — migrate both, leave no second copy) with a per-tile assessed sum over developed zone tiles, base(zone,lvl) × assessment(landv) × rate, accumulated in the O(n) pass deptCosts() already walks, and reshape the demand response into a continuous escalating penalty. THREE RATES ONLY IF SEPARABLE: demand.c is (pop*0.28-cJobs)/160 and demand.i is (pop*0.42-iJobs)/180 while demand.r keys on jobsAvail, so soaking industry kills iJobs, which kills jobsAvail, which kills residential demand — 'soak industry or subsidize it' may be an illusion the player discovers in an hour. Prove equilibrium separability before building three sliders; if it fails, ship the assessed base with one rate and record why. THE STABILIZER, WHICH NOBODY OWNED: once land value is the tax base, blight (GP10), low coverage and congestion become revenue holes that force service cuts that deepen the holes — a closed positive-feedback death spiral built from four milestones. This one owns the damper: an assessed-value floor per developed tile, an urban-renewal budget line the player funds, and a REAL debt ladder (BOND_PRINCIPAL/BOND_TERM/BOND_MAX are fixed constants at issueBond, sim.js:2058) with chooseable principal and term, a ceiling tied to the assessed base, and a credit rating with memory. Also tie road and service upkeep to SERVED LOAD, not only to building and tile counts as deptCosts() does today (sim.js:2120) — otherwise assessed revenue rising with land value hands an established city a permanent unattended surplus, regressing this dimension's own pass bar. Ship a wealth-band minimap overlay with an MM_LEGENDS entry and per-sector projected take. Save takes the next ladder integer; a legacy scalar taxRate loads into every rate.
milestones.player_facing_win: Parks, clean air, schools and transit finally show up as rent — raising land value literally pays the bills — and borrowing becomes a real instrument with a term, a ceiling and a reputation instead of one fixed button.
quality_gates: The spike is published first: a committed seed/size/script produces a documented equilibrium-revenue curve on the pre-change build and names which term binds (taxMod vs jobsAvail) with a measured sensitivity for each — the reference city is pinned before any formula changes.

Land value earns money: two cities with identical pop/jobs but mean landv differing by >=60 differ in monthly take by >=35%; the equilibrium-revenue curve on the PINNED reference city is single-peaked with an interior peak and equilibrium pop at 14% is >=20% below equilibrium pop at 3%.

Separability, or an honest single rate: raising only the industrial rate 6 points moves demand.i >=0.15 while demand.r moves <0.05 measured 120 rollovers AFTER the change (not instantaneously). If it fails, the milestone ships one rate and records the measurement — this gate passes either way but never ships three sliders that do the same thing.

No free surplus and the spiral is damped: an unattended established city's net over 240 rollovers stays within ±10% of zero at the calibrated rate; a city driven into a blight/revenue hole returns to solvency within 60 rollovers using the urban-renewal line and the bond ladder in >=8 of 10 seeded runs, with the assessed-value floor observed to bind (revenue never reaches zero while developed tiles remain).

Calibration and scenario safety: the pinned reference city at the legacy rate collects within ±10% of the GP6 baseline's monthly take; all 5 scenarios remain winnable in >=8 of 10 seeded reference playthroughs (Y2K Ready's 2500 pop + §4000 + power margin and Twister Season's pop>=4000 are calibrated against the old revenue math, and previously earned medals persist in localStorage via recordTrophy, scenarios.js:307).

Save-compat/determinism: a legacy scalar taxRate loads into every rate, resaves at the next ladder version, round-trips idempotently, and its next 120 rollovers match a native city built from the same state; the advisor projection at advisors.js:373/394 is migrated with no duplicate formula left behind; terrain and bakes stay byte-identical; zero console errors.
milestones.pre_split: Split at launch per S3: GP7a = the assessed-value SHADOW ledger — show what taxes WOULD be under assessed valuation next to actual, read-only, byte-identical. GP7b = the cutover + debt ladder + stabilizer, measured against GP7a projections.

milestones.title: Coupled Hazard, the Risk Readout & Emergency Response
milestones.scope: Effort re-rated 4->5 and explicitly three-phase, with phase 1 shippable on its own so a capped session still lands value. PHASE 1 — TWO SHIPPED DEFECTS, hours not days, and they must go first: register the four orphaned M29 disasters in MENUS.disasters (verified at ui.js:322 — only fire/tornado/UFO of seven kinds are listed, so four already-built, already-verified disasters are unreachable), and generalize scenario pressure off the hardcoded `sc.pressure.type === 'tornado'` (verified at scenarios.js:362) so every kind is usable as scenario pressure — with a real difficulty axis (frequency and severity settings), which the challenge pass bar demands and the draft only gestured at. PHASE 2 — HAZARD VECTOR + READOUT: replace the flat `Math.random() < 0.0009` roll (sim.js:2385; 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.8%/yr, arithmetically exact) with a monthly vector computed from state the sim already maintains — FIRE from fireCov shortfall x density x summer; RIOT from crime x unemployment x police funding (and this is where approval couples in, NOT in GP6); FLOOD from developed tiles within N of TERR.WATER x season; QUAKE a flat baseline; MELTDOWN from plantYear age on an OV.NUKE; MONSTER/UFO gated on pollution. Surface in a #dlg-civdef panel: per-hazard Low/Elevated/High/Severe meter, the single largest contributing factor named in plain English, and a live per-year odds figure. PHASE 3 — DISPATCH: while a disaster is active or any fire[] tile burns, an EMERGENCY toolbar mode offers an allowance derived from powered station anchors scaled by funding — engines knock fire[] down in a 1-tile radius and firebreak their tile, police squads multiply the polCov riot drain, a Metropolis-tier Guard unit shortens monster/tornado ticks. Each dispatch costs §; units expire with the event. SERIALIZATION, WHICH THE DRAFT GOT WRONG: 'the roster rides inside the already-conditionally-serialized this.disaster object so no version bump is needed' is broken for the 55%-likeliest disaster — startDisaster('fire') (sim.js:1798-1811) ignites a tile and RETURNS without ever setting this.disaster, and fire[] is not in serialize() at all, so saving mid-fire already silently loses the fire. This milestone serializes fire[] plus the roster and takes the next ladder integer; fixing the mid-fire save loss is a bonus bug fix, not optional. Ship a disaster Bugle front page, optional auto-pause + camera jump, and the advisors' first disaster lines.
milestones.player_facing_win: Disasters stop being arbitrary weather and become the itemized bill for decisions the player could see coming on a risk panel — and when one lands, the allowance is always smaller than the fire front, so the player must choose what to let burn.
quality_gates: Reachability and difficulty axis (phase 1, independently verifiable): all 7 disaster kinds launch from MENUS.disasters and are usable as a scenario pressure type at >=2 difficulty settings whose measured event frequency differs by >=2x; each kind publishes exactly one Bugle front page.
Coupling: across 10 seeded 50-year headless runs, a city with full fire coverage and funded police suffers >=50% fewer fires and >=70% fewer riots than a neglected city of equal population.

Honest meters: the panel's per-year odds match the measured empirical rate over 10 x 50-year runs within ±20%; each meter moves to the correct band within one rollover of the driving change (bulldoze all fire stations, age a nuke past PLANT_WARN_AGE); the named contributor is always the largest term in the vector.

Agency: dispatching the full allowance at a fire front cuts total tiles lost >=35% vs the same seeded fire with no dispatch; the allowance is strictly smaller than the front at peak in >=90% of sampled fires; § is charged correctly and every unit expires with the event.

Mid-event persistence (a fix, not a regression): saving during an active fire and reloading restores fire[] and the roster exactly and the event continues to an identical outcome; an in-progress disaster of every kind round-trips idempotently at the new ladder version.

No-regression/calibration: with disastersEnabled=false the city is byte-identical to the GP7 baseline across 600 ticks (the flag-off path draws zero hazard RNG, asserted by a call counter); a well-run city's aggregate annual disaster rate is at or below 23% and a neglected one is measurably above; all 5 scenarios remain winnable; zero console errors.
milestones.pre_split: Split at launch per S3: GP8a = the risk readout (per-tile hazard odds from coverage/pollution/plant age; read-only; its honesty gate = empirical disaster rates over a long soak match the displayed odds). GP8b = coupled hazard rates + the emergency-response allowance (behavior).

milestones.title: Garbage & Waste Management (M31) — Growth You Must Put Somewhere
milestones.scope: Ship the already-designed M31, with the two collisions the panel found priced into the effort (3->4). Zones generate garbage by activity (per-tile rate from zone type x lvl, industry heaviest), summed to a citywide tonnage against disposal capacity. Two routes with opposite costs: a paint-style LANDFILL (cheap per tile, per-cell capacity; saturating cells scar land value and emit a pollution source that persists after the cell is full) and a tier-gated WASTE-TO-ENERGY INCINERATOR (2x2, high capital, consumes a fixed tonnage, trickles power, smogs its own neighbourhood). A Recycling ordinance cuts the stream for a §/mo cost, joining the shipped ORDINANCES table. Overflow accumulates as an uncollected-garbage scalar driving a growing pollution source, complaint faxes on the existing click-to-jump path, and a land-value penalty. COLLISION 1: 'new OV ids round-trip for free' conflates SAVE round-trip with SIM neutrality. Any id >= OV.ZR automatically joins recomputePower's conducts (sim.js:905), brownout (924) and y2k (939) idioms and the fire-candidate scan (1803) — a paint-style LANDFILL sprayed over hundreds of tiles would conduct electricity across itself, register as a powered consumer, and be flammable. Add an isWaste() predicate applied at every one of those sites, following the isWaterOv (M24) and isMega (M28) precedent the codebase documents at sim.js:106-114, and extend the index-keyed ovName array (ui.js:1523). COLLISION 2: 'trickles power via the existing supply path' means joining isPlant(), which drags in plantYear stamping, the aging curve, PLANT_WARN_AGE nagging and the flat plants*40 upkeep, AND breaks powerMix()'s documented five-bucket Σ === powerSupply contract (sim.js:1050-1065) plus the budget power-mix panel. Decide in scope, not in implementation: add a sixth waste bucket to powerMix with its own upkeep, or thread a second supply channel. Ship a budget line for waste operations, a tonnage readout in the query panel, and a Garbage minimap overlay with an MM_LEGENDS entry (in GP5's regrouped strip). Landfill per-cell fill levels are the one new serialized array; save takes the next ladder integer.
milestones.player_facing_win: Growth now produces something the player must physically put somewhere — cheap landfill that poisons the ground it sits on, or an expensive incinerator that turns the problem into a trickle of power and a cloud over its own neighbourhood.
quality_gates: Stream scales with the city: generated tonnage is monotone in developed-zone count and level across 5 test cities, and a city with zero disposal accumulates overflow whose mean pollution rises >=20 within 24 rollovers.

The two routes genuinely differ: sufficient landfill capacity zeroes overflow but drops mean landv within 4 tiles of saturated cells by >=20; an equivalent-capacity incinerator leaves neighbourhood landv intact (<5 drop at equal distance), adds pollution at its own site, and contributes its rated MW to powerSupply.

Anti-crosstalk audit passes: waste ids conduct no power, register no power demand, are not brownout/y2k/fire candidates, and resolve to a name in ovName — asserted individually at sim.js:905, 924, 939 and 1803 — and powerMix's buckets still sum EXACTLY to powerSupply with an incinerator on the grid.

Saturation and ordinance: a full landfill cell accepts no further tonnage, renders visibly distinct, reports 'full' in the query panel, and total city capacity equals the sum over unsaturated cells; enabling Recycling cuts generated tonnage by the designed percentage ±2% and posts a non-zero §/mo in the ordinance row.

Save-compat: older saves load with zero garbage state and no retroactive overflow penalty; the landfill fill array round-trips idempotently at the new ladder version; a loaded city's next 120 rollovers match a native equivalent byte-for-byte.

Determinism/no-regression: same seed + script reproduces identical garbage, overflow and pollution series over 600 ticks with Math.random unstubbed; a city with no waste buildings is byte-identical to the GP8 baseline; all 5 scenarios remain winnable; zero console errors.
milestones.launch_note: Waste chain per original M31 design; S4 applies — garbage must be visible (landfill fill states, truck traffic on load[]).

milestones.title: Blight & Urban Renewal — Decline With a Campaign Against It
milestones.scope: Demoted to last and REWRITTEN against two objections the panel proved. OBJECTION 1 — the counting substrate does not exist. The draft specified 'a per-tile abandon counter alongside the existing unpow[] idiom' counting 'N consecutive MONTH ROLLOVERS', but unpow[] rides growthPass's 340-random-tile sampler (sim.js:1676-1678): at 24 ticks/month that is roughly 1.27 Poisson-distributed samples per tile per month on an 80x80 map, so a per-tile consecutive-months counter cannot ride it at all. Add a NEW deterministic O(n) monthly sweep — which is also exactly what the '18 consecutive rollovers -> >=60% abandoned' gate requires. Effort 3->4. OBJECTION 2 — as drafted this was punishment with no decision: the player's entire move set was 'bulldoze (pay, click)' or 'wait out a recovery window', and the scope called a cooldown 'a real campaign'. Ship abandonment TOGETHER with the tools to fight it: an urban-renewal district designation funded from the budget line GP7 created (accelerates recovery while it costs §/mo), a mass clear-and-rezone tool priced below individual bulldozing, and a redevelopment ordinance. Recovery becomes something the player RUNS. MECHANICS: a developed zone spending N consecutive monthly sweeps under failing conditions (unpowered, deeply negative sector demand, crime above threshold, repeated gridlock eviction) flips to ABANDONED — a flag beside over[], preserving zone type and district assignment. An abandoned tile contributes zero pop/jobs/tax, emits crime and a small pollution source, drags neighbourhood landv, and refuses to redevelop until conditions have been clear for the recovery window. Distinct derelict sprite (boarded windows, no night glow) from the existing procedural pipeline; ticker line and a complaint kind on the shipped click-to-jump path; 'Abandoned lots' in the almanac and district stats; a new entry in GP1's gate table so blight ships with its own tile verdict for free. This milestone closes the loop GP7's stabilizer damps and therefore ships after it by construction — its gates must prove the spiral is survivable, not merely that it exists.
milestones.player_facing_win: Neglect finally costs something — a neighbourhood can die and sit as a blighted hole dragging its neighbours down — but the mayor has a renewal campaign to run against it rather than a timer to wait out.
quality_gates: Causation on a deterministic sweep: a district cut off from power for 18 consecutive month rollovers has >=60% of its developed tiles abandoned while an identical powered control has 0; a visit counter proves the sweep touches every tile exactly once per rollover and draws zero RNG for the counter itself.
Hysteresis: restoring power does not immediately revive — measured revival latency is within ±2 rollovers of the designed window across 20 seeded runs.

Blight radiates and the campaign beats waiting: mean landv within 4 tiles of an abandoned cluster drops >=15 vs control and crime rises; funding the urban-renewal designation restores that cluster to within 5% of control landv at least 40% faster than doing nothing, at a measurable and reported § cost.

The spiral is survivable: from a scripted worst case (power loss into a revenue hole into service cuts), a competent scripted recovery returns the city to solvency and rising pop within 60 rollovers in >=8 of 10 seeded runs, with GP7's assessed-value floor observed to bind (monthly revenue never reaches zero while developed tiles remain).

Census integrity and legibility: abandoned tiles contribute 0 pop, 0 jobs and 0 tax at every sampled rollover and city.pop equals the recomputed sum over non-abandoned tiles; diagnoseTile returns the abandonment verdict for every abandoned tile with its recovery countdown as evidence.

Save-compat/determinism: older saves load with the abandon array all-zero and no retroactive blight; the new ladder version round-trips idempotently; a loaded healthy city's next 120 rollovers match a native equivalent byte-for-byte; same seed + script reproduces identical abandon evolution over 600 ticks; all 5 scenarios remain winnable; zero console errors.
milestones.launch_note: Last: consumes strain/blight substrates from GP5/GP6. S4: blight must be visible tile-by-tile, and the renewal campaign paints visibly back.

reconcile_changelog: ADDED A MILESTONE THAT DID NOT EXIST: Expressways, Ramps & the First Moving Train (now rank 4). The fun lens's strongest finding was that the draft added exactly two buildable things (landfill, incinerator) against four new friction systems, and that the commute milestone creates a bottleneck problem while its own scope defers the only tool that answers it. A road class hierarchy with ramps and a real siting penalty is the SC2K layout dilemma; the animated train closes the aliveness guard's 'N/A until a train ships' slot. This is the one new toy in ranks 1-4.

DROPPED 'Offers & Ultimatums' (old GP9) entirely to make room. Three grounds, all verified: the Federal Prison is a placeable building smuggled into an events table (recomputeDemand consumes only additive demandR/C/I types at sim.js:1509-1513 — there is no spatial modifier channel), full-information binary modals are solved once and become autopilot forever after, and it hard-depended on the ports milestone. Its best idea (state-triggered rather than calendar-triggered pressure) is preserved in the hazard vector's coupling to live state.

PROMOTED the seeded RNG stream from 'a prerequisite milestone the roadmap does not contain' into rank 1 alongside the verdict engine — same surgery, same function. Verified the panel's load-bearing falsehood claim: 46 raw Math.random() calls in js/sim.js cover the whole tick path (growth sampling and rolls, traffic reservoir picks at 1267, road wear 1318, fire spread 1774/1786, disaster roll 2385) while mulberry32 (sim.js:463) serves only terrain and neighbor personalities. Every 'byte-identical' gate in the draft inherited that fragility. Rank 1 now declares the ONE authorized re-pin and makes every later identity gate mean something.

RESTRUCTURED rank 1 from a hard-coded seven-code enumeration into a DECLARATIVE GATE TABLE that growthPass itself consumes. The fun lens showed diagnoseTile would otherwise be rewritten three times (strain gate, job-reach gate, abandoned state), invalidating its own gate each time. Now a new gate cannot ship without its verdict, and three later milestones get their tile verdicts for free.

FIXED the rank-1 verdict set: added the burning-tile check (sim.js:1682, precedes everything), the demand-below-0.15 threshold (sim.js:1701 — the commonest real stall, previously reported as 'growing normally'), and the negligible-fit-odds code (sim.js:1704-1712; a headless rig showed demand.r at 0.78-1.00 with pop flat, i.e. fit was binding, not the enumerated gates). Corrected the water cap's precedence — it fires at lvl >= 1, so it pre-empts the level-2 service cap. Replaced the self-referential '7/7 codes' gate with a differential fuzz against an instrumented growthPass.

CORRECTED the rank-1 drag premise: drags do NOT truncate silently — place() returns {ok:false,reason:'funds'} (sim.js:764) and applyToolAt already plays Snd.denied() with '⛔ Not enough funds!' (ui.js:614). The meter is now a preview that must not be stricter than the budget, since collectBudget can legitimately push funds negative. Also gave the hover readout its own status cell with a message TTL, because a per-pixel mousemove into #sb-tool (index.html:122) would erase transient warnings before they are read.

ADDED RCI decomposition to rank 1. The feedback pass bar demands gauges decompose into named signed contributors; demand.r is literally a sum of six named terms sitting in recomputeDemand (sim.js:1503-1520) and nothing in the draft exposed them. Cheap, and it closes a self-declared pass bar the draft left unmet.

PROMOTED Working Ports 4 -> 2. All three lenses independently asked for this. sim.js:55-64 documents in the code's own words that AIRPORT and SEAPORT 'deliberately join NO predicate — behaves exactly like OV.STADIUM'. Dead content on the two most expensive buildings is bug-shaped work and outranks new systems under a cap. Effort re-rated 2 -> 3 for the directional noise map.

PROMOTED Commute & Job Access 7 -> 3, splitting the difference between the fun lens (rank 2) and the two lenses that wanted it held back. It is the only milestone delivering the north star's central claim, and shipping it before the strain/blight/tax work means those are written once against the final growth model instead of three times against a doomed one. Fixed two defects: the strictly-downhill walk would collapse all trips onto one canonical corridor (now weighted among equal-or-lower neighbours from the seeded stream, with a non-degeneracy gate), and 'C/I trips keep the legacy walk so the change stays surgical' was false pre-rank-1 because both drew from the same interleaved global stream.

DEMOTED Assessed-Value Taxation 2 -> 7 on unanimous panel advice, and corrected its diagnosis. sim.js:1503 is `taxMod = (7 - this.taxRate) * 0.05` — strictly LINEAR, not the 'flat-then-cliff' the draft described. A headless R-heavy rig already produces a single-peaked curve peaking at 7% that would PASS the draft's own Laffer gate on HEAD; only a serviced balanced rig shows the degenerate 'set 13% and win'. The milestone now leads with a measurement spike on a PINNED reference city and will ship one rate rather than three fake ones if equilibrium separability fails through the jobsAvail chain.

GAVE THE DEATH SPIRAL AN OWNER. Four milestones (assessed-value tax, blight, approval, hazard) closed a positive-feedback loop nobody stabilized. The taxation milestone now owns an assessed-value floor, an urban-renewal budget line, and the real debt ladder the economy pass bar demands (BOND_PRINCIPAL/BOND_TERM/BOND_MAX are fixed constants at sim.js:2058) — plus consumption-scaled upkeep, without which assessed revenue would hand an established city a permanent unattended surplus and regress that pass bar.

ADDED THE MISSING PROGRESSION RUNG to the approval milestone. TIERS (sim.js:236-242) is five raw population thresholds topping out at Metropolis/5000 and no milestone in the draft touched it, so economy-progression could not reach its own pass bar. Megalopolis is now gated on population AND sustained approval AND a commute/pollution condition — earned by governing, not by zoning.

ADDED THE EDUCATION PAYOFF to the service-strain milestone, converting it from a pure cost increase into an investment. Verified sim.js:1392 and 1709 SUM eduCov and medCov and 1721 ORs them, so per-department capacity alone could not meet the 'education and health are mechanically distinct with different payoffs' pass bar. Crime, pollution, tax and coverage already suppress growth through landv and fit; damping demand.r on top double-charges the same neglect and muddies the causal chain the milestone exists to clarify. Also resolved its two self-contradictions: the EMA is path-dependent by construction so the 'pure function of serialized state' gate is gone, and 'simulates identically outside the approval channel' was impossible while approval fed back into the sim.

RESOLVED THE VERSION COLLISION. Six milestones each independently declared 'save v12' with 'v11 loads'. Rank 1 now owns v12 and establishes an explicit ladder: every later state-adding milestone takes the next integer and the loader maintains a v11..vN migration chain. Under a stop-anywhere cap the ladder rule holds regardless of which milestones actually ship.

Verified sim.js:16-22 builds a fresh object from a hardcoded 7-key list and DROPS unknown keys — the draft's claims that it 'already tolerates the new key' were wrong in the direction that silently destroys an approval or commute series on every load. Both milestones adding a series now name the edit and gate on a round-trip with zero dropped points.

SPLIT AND RE-RATED the civil-defense milestone (effort 4 -> 5, three phases with phase 1 shippable alone) and fixed its broken serialization claim. startDisaster('fire') (sim.js:1798-1811) ignites and RETURNS without ever setting this.disaster — fire is 55% of the roll — and fire[] is not in serialize() at all, so saving mid-fire already silently loses the fire. The roster cannot ride inside this.disaster; fire[] and the roster are serialized and the mid-fire save loss is fixed as a bonus. Phase 1 is the two shipped defects (four disasters unreachable from MENUS.disasters at ui.js:322, hardcoded 'tornado' pressure at scenarios.js:362) plus a real scenario difficulty axis.

PRICED THE OV-ID CROSSTALK into the waste milestone (effort 3 -> 4) and applied the same audit to the new expressway ids. 'over[] is a Uint8Array so new ids round-trip for free' is true for SAVE and false for SIM: any id >= OV.ZR joins recomputePower's conducts (905), brownout (924) and y2k (939) idioms and the fire-candidate scan (1803) — a paint-style landfill would conduct electricity across itself and be flammable. Both milestones now carry an explicit predicate task following the isWaterOv/isMega precedent documented at sim.js:106-114, plus the ovName extension at ui.js:1523, and the waste milestone must decide the powerMix sixth-bucket question rather than assume the isPlant() path is free (it breaks the documented Σ === powerSupply contract at sim.js:1050-1065).

Its counting substrate did not exist — unpow[] rides a 340-random-tile sampler giving ~1.27 Poisson samples per tile per month, so a consecutive-months counter cannot ride it; it now specifies a deterministic O(n) monthly sweep. And it shipped punishment with no decision ('a real campaign' that was actually a cooldown), so the renewal tools now ship with it and its gates prove the spiral is survivable rather than merely that it exists.

At school ~500 / hospital ~800 / police ~1200 / fire ~1500, any baseline city large enough to be interesting is already strained, so 'byte-identical wherever capacity >= load' only held for toy cities. Nothing in the draft checked this, yet the tax reshape, service strain, commute gating and blight each independently suppress equilibrium growth and stack multiplicatively — while Twister Season requires pop >= 4000 and Y2K Ready 2500 pop + §4000 + a power margin, and medals persist across cities in localStorage (recordTrophy, scenarios.js:307), making previously earned golds unreproducible.

process_scaffolding: S1 BASELINE LEDGER: every commit that changes what is live in the tree updates baseline_ledger in the same commit. A workflow brief always quotes the ledger, never memory.

S2 TWO-STRIKE SPLIT: a milestone refuted twice is never attempted a third time whole — it is split (read-surfaces half vs behavior half) or blocked for a user decision. Splitting GP1 is what made GP1a byte-identical-provable.

S3 READ-FIRST SPLITS: instrumentation and player-facing readouts ship BEFORE the behavior they describe. The read half carries a byte-identical gate; the behavior half re-pins against it and is measured by the instrumentation the read half proved honest.

S4 SIM-ART COHERENCE (the SC2K bar): every new sim state must have a visible expression, consistent at all 4 rotations, and every failure state must be visually distinct from its working state. In actual SimCity 2000 nothing invisible ever bills the player. (Lesson: dead port identical to a working one; noise cone perpendicular to the drawn runway.)

S5 OUTCOME GATES FOR THE ECONOMY: never gate on instantaneous demand deltas — demand is a self-correcting pressure signal, so an additive bonus is absorbed into growth. Gate on OUTCOMES over a horizon vs a control city: built development, census jobs, realized revenue.

S6 INTEGRITY: implement-phase self-assessment never stands as certification (twice caught false); workers never amend a gate so work passes it — mis-specified gates are reported and decided by the user; agent-set statuses are reverted pending independent verification.
S7 LIVENESS: the driving loop checks transcript mtime + worker processes every firing; a stale-25-min workflow is resumed from cache, never waited on.
S8 INDEPENDENT SHIPPABILITY: stopping between any two items leaves a coherent, certified, published game.
